title: Multi-Time States in Quantum and Operational Probabilistic Theories: An Axiomatic Framework
authors: Kaumudibikash Goswami, Archana Barvar, Manabendra Nath Bera
abstract: Quantum states over time were introduced, in part, to extend Bayesian probability to quantum theory and have since found applications across diverse areas, ranging from quantum causality and open-system dynamics to tests of macroscopic realism. While axiomatic characterizations of these states exist for Markovian dynamics, a general framework accommodating non-Markovian dynamics is still lacking. Moreover, extending this framework beyond quantum mechanics to general physical theories also remains elusive. In this work, we develop an axiomatic framework for multi-time states within a class of operational probabilistic theories (OPTs) that includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Based on three assumptions---compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency---the framework accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics, and provides sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory within OPT. As a concrete application of our OPT framework, we fully characterize the unique multi-time state in boxworld and develop a method for Bayesian retrodiction of physical transformations there. Our general framework is consistent with quantum theory, reproducing several existing results. In the non-Markovian quantum dynamics, we establish a correspondence between multi-time states and the process-matrix framework, and fully characterize the multi-time states compatible with general dynamics. This correspondence also lets us infer quantum causal models from multi-time states, and as a proof of principle, we propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order from quantum multi-time states. These results provide a unified framework for studying spatio-temporal states, causal relations, and Bayesian reasoning within OPTs, with implications for both fundamental and applied research.
summary: This paper constructs a general axiomatic framework for multi-time states applicable to Operational Probabilistic Theories (OPTs), generalizing concepts beyond standard quantum mechanics. By imposing axioms like compositionality, it successfully models both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics. The resulting framework unifies the study of spatio-temporal states, causality, and Bayesian reasoning across diverse physical theories.
main_problem: The paper aims to develop a general axiomatic framework for characterizing multi-time states that extends beyond quantum mechanics to a broader class of Operational Probabilistic Theories (OPTs). It seeks to provide a unified understanding of spatio-temporal states and causality in general physical theories.
main_result: The framework successfully accommodates both Markovian and non-Markovian dynamics within OPTs, providing sufficient conditions to certify signaling and temporal memory. It establishes a correspondence between multi-time states and process-matrix frameworks for non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
method: The authors develop the framework using three core axioms: compositionality, reconstructibility, and spatio-temporal marginal consistency. They apply these axioms to characterize multi-time states and propose a semidefinite program to infer causal order.
model_or_system: The primary model is the Operational Probabilistic Theory (OPT), which includes quantum mechanics as a special case. Applications include characterizing multi-time states in 'boxworld' and analyzing general non-Markovian quantum dynamics.
key_observables: Multi-time states (MTSs), signaling, temporal memory, and causal order.
important_parameters: The framework is general, but specific applications involve characterizing dynamics across time steps (Markovian vs. non-Markovian).
main_assumptions: The framework assumes the underlying theory is an OPT with finite-dimensional convex state spaces, causality, and local tomography.
paper_structure: The paper builds from the general axiomatic definition of MTSs in OPTs, applies these axioms to characterize dynamics (Markovian/non-Markovian), and then details specific applications like the boxworld model and the correspondence with process matrices.
why_interesting: This work provides a highly abstract, foundational framework for understanding time evolution and causality in quantum and non-quantum systems, which is crucial for developing generalized theories of open quantum systems.
